title: JsonDB.dump() leaves db_file unbound in finally block when open() fails, masking the original exception
claim: If open() raises (permission error, disk full, etc.), db_file is never assigned. The finally clause then raises NameError/UnboundLocalError, replacing and masking the original OS error.

title: get_module() captures initial_workdir in a module-level global instead of returning it
claim: global initial_workdir; initial_workdir = os.getcwd() writes call-history-dependent state into a module global; any code that calls get_module() more than once observes whichever invocation ran last.

title: get_module() changes the process-wide CWD via os.chdir without restoring it on failure
claim: os.chdir(full_cwd) modifies the CWD for the entire process and is never restored in a finally block; if importlib.import_module raises, the CWD is left changed, breaking all subsequent relative-path resolution.

title: get_module() permanently grows sys.path on every call, including when the call ultimately fails
claim: sys.path.insert(0, base_path) (and a potential second insert for full_cwd) is never cleaned up; every call, successful or not, permanently lengthens sys.path, causing import shadowing and making later imports depend on call order.

title: _CMDLINE_VARS is a module-level mutable global that causes state corruption under concurrent or successive runs
claim: The None sentinel and reset_vars() pattern share global state across successive DoitMain().run() calls and across threads/processes, producing silent wrong defaults with no diagnostic when the variable is read before it is initialised.

title: Dependency.get_value() raises bare Exception instead of a specific DependencyError subclass
claim: Two raise Exception(...) calls (acknowledged by a FIXME comment) prevent callers from distinguishing a legitimate missing-value lookup from a programming error without parsing message strings.

title: CmdAction.execute() opens os.devnull for suppressed output but never closes the file handle
claim: open(os.devnull, 'w') is called but the returned file object is never closed; repeated actions with capture_io=None accumulate file descriptors until GC or process termination, potentially exhausting the OS limit.

title: DoitConfig.load_config_toml uses assert to validate plugin_type, which is silently stripped by python -O
claim: assert plugin_type in self.PLUGIN_TYPES disappears under -O/-OO, allowing an invalid plugin type to pass silently into the configuration with no error message.

title: CmdAction.execute() inserts PYTHONUNBUFFERED into the caller's original env dictionary
claim: pkwargs is shallow-copied but the nested env dict is not; env['PYTHONUNBUFFERED'] = '1' modifies the original dictionary owned by the caller, silently changing the behaviour of any subsequent reuse of that dictionary.

title: CmdAction.execute() conflates an explicitly empty env dict with a missing one via 'if not env'
claim: if not env is True for both None and {}, so an intentionally empty environment supplied by the caller is replaced with the full parent environment (os.environ.copy()) instead of being preserved.

title: get_module() imports task files by basename, allowing sys.modules cache to return the wrong module for same-named files in different directories
claim: Two files such as /project-a/dodo.py and /project-b/dodo.py share the module name 'dodo'; loading the second in the same interpreter can return the first cached module from sys.modules, producing an order-dependent, hard-to-reproduce failure.

title: load_tasks() raises IndexError on an empty argument string due to unchecked term[0] access
claim: for index, term in enumerate(args): if term[0] != '-' raises IndexError when term is an empty string; callers should receive a meaningful parse error rather than an internal traceback.

title: JsonDB.dump() truncates the DB file before encoding completes, leaving it empty on serialisation failure
claim: open(self.name, 'w') immediately truncates the on-disk file to zero bytes; if self.codec.encode(self._db) subsequently raises, the file is left empty and the database is permanently corrupted.

title: PythonAction.pm_pdb is a class-level attribute mutated at runtime, causing a race condition under MThreadRunner
claim: pm_pdb = False is a class attribute; cmd_run.py sets it with PythonAction.pm_pdb = pdb before each run, modifying the class itself so concurrent threads may observe an inconsistent value and the attribute is never reset.

title: Task.__init__ mutates the caller's uptodate list in-place via extend()
claim: uptodate.extend(self._init_getargs()) modifies the list supplied by the caller; reusing the same task definition dict can therefore accumulate extra checks or produce different tasks on later calls.

title: PluginEntry.load misreports an ImportError raised inside an existing plugin as 'module not found'
claim: Catching bare ImportError conflates a missing module with a broken dependency inside an already-found module; the useful exception chain is discarded and the diagnostic message is inaccurate.

title: PluginEntry.load raises generic Exception for both module-not-found and attribute-not-found failures
claim: Both error branches raise generic Exception, preventing callers from classifying failure without parsing message strings; a dedicated PluginLoadError with exception chaining would enable programmatic handling.

title: DoitMain.process_args raises IndexError on an empty command-line argument string via unchecked arg[0]
claim: arg[0] is accessed without a length guard; an empty string—valid in some shell or API contexts—raises IndexError instead of a controlled parse error.

title: DumpDB.execute() opens the DBM dependency database without a context manager, risking unreleased file locks
claim: dbm.open(dep_file) is called without a with-statement; a DBM backend can retain file descriptors and locks until GC, preventing subsequent commands from reopening or replacing the dependency database.

title: CmdParse.parse_only() catches bare Exception instead of getopt.GetoptError, converting internal bugs into misleading parse errors
claim: Catching Exception converts bugs in option construction, unexpected input types, and internal failures into misleading 'invalid command line' messages; narrow catches preserve tracebacks for actual defects.

title: CmdParse.parse_only() does not chain the caught exception when raising CmdParseError, discarding the low-level cause
claim: raise CmdParseError(msg) without 'from error' discards the original exception from the chain, reducing diagnostic information available to callers and debuggers.

title: DbmDB.set() initialises an empty dict for a task_id not yet in cache, silently overwriting persistent data on dump
claim: If a task exists in persistent storage but has not been read into the in-memory cache, set() starts with {} and on dump() replaces the complete stored record, silently discarding other dependency states and saved values.

title: SqliteDB.set() initialises an empty dict for a task_id not yet in cache, silently overwriting persistent data on dump
claim: Same data-integrity bug as DbmDB.set: if a task exists in persistent storage but has not been read into _cache, set() starts with {} and on dump() replaces the complete stored record, silently discarding other dependency states.

title: PythonAction.execute() redirects sys.stdout/sys.stderr before the try/finally that restores them, leaving streams corrupted if _prepare_kwargs() raises
claim: _prepare_kwargs() executes after replacing sys.stdout and sys.stderr but before entering the protected try/finally; if it raises, the streams are never restored, permanently corrupting process-global I/O.

title: Many classes and methods lack proper docstrings
claim: Many classes and methods lack proper docstrings, reducing maintainability and IDE tooltip support; normalize_callable's existing docstring is minimal and does not document arguments, return value, or examples.

title: get_file_md5 uses javadoc-style @param/@return tags inconsistent with Python conventions
claim: get_file_md5 uses @param and @return tags from the epydoc/javadoc tradition, inconsistent with standard Python docstring conventions (Google, NumPy, or reStructuredText style).

title: Magic number 128 used as block-size multiplier in get_file_md5 without explanation
claim: block_size = 128 * md5.block_size uses a magic number whose origin and intent are not obvious, making maintenance harder.

title: Error message construction in check_attr uses old-style % formatting
claim: The error message in check_attr uses old-style % string formatting, which is less readable and maintainable than f-strings.

title: _init_uptodate method is overly complex with multiple nested conditionals
claim: _init_uptodate has complex nested conditionals with multiple paths that violate single responsibility and make the method hard to test and maintain.

title: expand_action() hardcodes self.STRING_FORMAT = 'old' inside the method body, overriding any prior configuration
claim: self.STRING_FORMAT = 'old' is assigned inside expand_action(), so the format is always forced to 'old' regardless of what was previously configured, making the choice inflexible.

title: DbmDB.in_() method appears to be defined twice in the same class body
claim: The in_() method is defined twice in DbmDB; Python silently overwrites the first definition with the second, and the duplication increases maintenance burden.

title: Comment in get_state describes what the code does rather than why
claim: The comment restates the if-condition rather than explaining why timestamp equality is a sufficient proxy for content equality and what its limits are.

title: Test injects command-line arguments via patch.object(sys, 'argv'), indicating over-coupling to CLI parsing
claim: Using patch.object(sys, 'argv', ...) to inject arguments indicates the system is overly coupled to CLI parsing rather than exposing a testable programmatic API.

title: get_module() mixes file system I/O operations with module loading logic
claim: get_module mixes path validation, sys.path manipulation, and os.chdir with the core logic of loading a Python module, making the function impure and harder to test in isolation.

title: doit/__init__.py uses assert to suppress a pyflakes warning about load_ipython_extension
claim: assert load_ipython_extension suppresses a pyflakes warning at the cost of a runtime assert that disappears under -O; import-time side effects and runtime assertions should not be used as a linting workaround.

title: DoitConfig initialises configuration eagerly at construction time rather than at point of use
claim: DoitConfig is not lazy in loading configuration files, meaning failures in config file reading occur at initialisation time rather than when configuration values are first needed.

title: Tests use temporary files and real DB implementations where isolation from file I/O would be preferable
claim: Heavy use of temporary files and real DB implementations complicates running individual tests and slows the test suite; an in-memory DB stub would provide better isolation.

title: Tests use patch to mock MRunner.available, indicating I/O is too tightly coupled with logic
claim: Extensive use of patch.object(runner.MRunner, 'available', ...) signals that runner availability is not injectable as a dependency, forcing monkey-patching in tests.

title: DoitMain.run() mixes argument processing, command dispatch, and error handling in a single method
claim: DoitMain.run() has too much imperative control flow mixing argument processing, command selection, and error handling in one method, making individual pieces difficult to test without extensive mocking.

title: flat_generator function lacks an underscore prefix to indicate it is an internal helper
claim: flat_generator should use an underscore prefix to clearly signal that it is an internal helper not part of the public API.

title: isinstance checks for str/PurePath targets could be simplified with a more Pythonic approach
claim: The two-branch isinstance check for string and PurePath targets can be collapsed into a single branch, reducing branching and making the intent clearer.

title: DoitMain.run() uses bare except Exception without logging, hiding diagnostic information
claim: The bare except Exception without logging means unexpected failures are written to stderr as raw tracebacks rather than captured by the logging system, reducing observability.

title: Task.__init__ uses a multi-line if/else for a simple conditional assignment
claim: if actions is None: self._actions = [] else: self._actions = list(actions[:]) is a style inconsistency; a ternary expression is more idiomatic for this simple conditional assignment.

title: _init_uptodate() does not wrap per-item processing in try/except, producing unclear tracebacks on failure
claim: Unexpected exceptions from configure_task calls or tuple indexing produce internal tracebacks rather than an InvalidTask message with context about which uptodate item caused the failure.

title: Task class docstring uses javadoc-style @ivar tags inconsistent with standard Python conventions
claim: The Task class docstring uses @ivar tags from the epydoc/javadoc tradition, inconsistent with standard Python docstring conventions and preventing proper documentation generation and IDE support.
